texts.preamble: Premlal Yadav vs The State Of M.P. on 16 January, 2020 Author: Vishnu Pratap Singh Chauhan Bench: Vishnu Pratap Singh Chauhan 1 Cr.R.No.415/2000 High Court Of Madhya Pradesh : Jabalpur Criminal Revision No.415/2000 Premlal Yadav -V/s- State of Madhya Pradesh ................................................................................. Present :- Hon'ble Shri Justice Vishnu Pratap Singh Chauhan ................................................................................. Shri S. K. Singh, counsel for the applicant. Shri Ashok Singh, Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State. ................................................................................. O R D E R
texts.facts: and one thousand rupees fine, with default stipulation. 2. The case of the prosecution against the applicant in short is that applicant was having mixed milk in the container and going to sell and distribute mixed milk, food inspector J. P. Verma introduced himself and purchased mixed milk from the applicant, mixed the same with formalin, prepared three samples and after performing all the formalities sent one sample to the public analyst State Food Laboratory and State Food Laboratory found the mixed milk adulterated and not found as per standard laid down under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955. The Food Inspector after being given notice to the applicant submitted a complaint before the Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class. 3. The applicant being aggrieved by that conviction and sentence preferred an appeal which was registered as Criminal Appeal No.124/1997. Hence, the applicant filed this criminal revision being aggrieved by that conviction and sentence passed by both the Courts below solely on the ground that learned trial Court not appreciated the evidence in proper perspective. Independent witness Rajendra Prasad not supported the case of prosecution and denied for the purchase of milk by food inspector. Food Inspector had not complied with the provision of Section 13(2) of the PFA Act. It is the mandatory provision. The judgment of both the Courts below have committed legal and factual error,hence, it has been prayed to allow this petition and acquit the applicant of the said charges. There was public analyst report on the record. Specific notice of 13(2) of the PFA Act had been sent to the applicant on the registered address but applicant had received that notice. Learned trial Court presumed the service of that notice. This witness categorically stated that after preparing one sample sent to the public analyst by registered post along with form no.7.This witness categorically exhibited public analyst report as Ex.P/13. On these specification public analyst found the sample adulterated.
texts.arguments: 4. Learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State on the other hand submitted that the appellate Court affirmed the conviction and sentence. It is a concurrent finding. 9. Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kishan Rao vs. Shankargouda, (2018) 8 SCC 165, while reiterating the ambit and scope of re-appreciation of evidence under Section 397 read with 401 of Cr.P.C. when conviction and sentence affirmed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge in appeal, has held in paras 12 to 14 as hereunder: 12. In State of Kerala vs. Puttumana Illath Jathavedan Namboodiri , 1999 (2) SCC 452, while considering the scope of the revisional jurisdiction of the High Court this Court has laid down the following: "5......In its revisional jurisdiction, the High Court can call for and examine the record of any proceedings for the purpose of satisfying itself as to the correctness, legality or propriety of any finding, sentence or order. Premlal Yadav vs The State Of M.P. on 16 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152767904/ 3 13. Another judgment which has also been referred to and relied by the High Court is the judgment of this Court in Sanjaysinh Ramrao Chavan vs. Dattatray Gulabrao Phalke and others, 2015 (3) SCC 123. This Court held that the High Court in exercise of revisional jurisdiction shall not interfere with the order of the Magistrate unless it is perverse or wholly unreasonable or there is non- consideration of any relevant material, the order cannot be [LEAKAGE_MASK] merely on the ground that another view is possible. Following has been laid down in paragraph 14: "14.....Unless the order passed by the Magistrate is perverse or the view taken by the court is wholly unreasonable or there is non- consideration of any relevant material or there is palpable misreading of records, the Revisional Court is not justified in setting aside the order, merely because another view is possible. Unless the finding of the court, whose decision is sought to be revised, is shown to be perverse or untenable in law or is grossly erroneous or glaringly unreasonable or where the decision is based on no material or where the material facts are wholly ignored or where the judicial discretion is exercised arbitrarily or capriciously, the courts may not interfere with decision in exercise of their revisional jurisdiction."
